questions.stem: Water has a specific heat capacity of 4200 J/(kg degrees C) and copper has 390 J/(kg degrees C). If equal masses receive the same energy, which heats up more?

options.text: Water, because it has a higher specific heat capacity
Copper, because it has a lower specific heat capacity
Both heat up by the same amount

questions.explanation: A lower specific heat capacity means less energy is needed per degree of temperature rise. So for the same energy input, copper's temperature rises much more than water's. This is why metals feel hot quickly when heated.
